new-york.name: Times Square
new-york.summary: The neon crossroads of Broadway and Seventh Avenue, ringed by giant screens and the theatres of the Broadway district.
new-york.expect: Crowded day and night, with costumed characters who expect tips for photos.
new-york.tip: See it after dark, then walk one block west for cheaper food on Ninth Avenue.
new-york.why: It has been the city's showplace since the 1900s and is the heart of the Broadway theatre district.
flow: Arrive from Bryant Park along 42nd Street.
Climb the red TKTS steps for the view up Broadway.
Catch a show or walk on to Hell's Kitchen for dinner.
new-york.bestFor: First-time visitors and Broadway theatre nights

new-york.name: Empire State Building
new-york.summary: The 1931 Art Deco skyscraper with open-air decks on the 86th floor and a glassed-in 102nd-floor observatory.
new-york.expect: Timed entry and security queues; the second-floor exhibits lead up to the lifts.
new-york.tip: Go late evening when the city lights come on; the 86th-floor deck is included, the 102nd costs extra.
new-york.why: It was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years and remains the most famous on the skyline.
flow: Enter on 34th Street with a timed ticket.
Walk through the exhibits to the express lifts.

new-york.name: Museum of Modern Art
new-york.summary: One of the world's great modern art collections, from Van Gogh's Starry Night and Monet's Water Lilies to Warhol and Pollock.
new-york.expect: Busy galleries on the fifth floor around the most famous works; the sculpture garden is a calm break.
new-york.tip: Start on the fifth floor at opening time and work downwards before the crowds arrive.
new-york.why: MoMA defined how the world collects and shows modern art, and its holdings span every major movement since the 1880s.
flow: Head straight to the fifth floor for 1880s–1940s.
Work down through the fourth and second floors.
Finish in the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Sculpture Garden.

new-york.name: Grand Central Terminal
new-york.summary: The 1913 Beaux-Arts railway terminal with its celestial ceiling, golden clock and whispering gallery.
new-york.expect: A working station, free to enter; rush hours bring commuters through the main concourse.
new-york.tip: Try the Whispering Gallery outside the Oyster Bar, then look up at the constellations on the ceiling.
new-york.why: Saved from demolition in the 1970s, it helped start America's historic preservation movement.
flow: Enter from 42nd Street into the main concourse.
Look up at the ceiling and the clock.
Find the Whispering Gallery on the lower level.
new-york.bestFor: A quick, free stop in Midtown

new-york.name: American Museum of Natural History
new-york.summary: A huge natural history museum facing Central Park, with dinosaur halls, the blue whale and the Rose Center planetarium.
new-york.expect: Very busy with families at weekends; pick a few halls rather than trying to see everything.
new-york.tip: Enter from Central Park West and go straight up to the fourth-floor dinosaur halls.
new-york.why: Its fossil and dioramas collections are among the largest in the world.
flow: See the Hall of Ocean Life and the blue whale.
End at the Gilder Center or the Rose Center planetarium.
